runs.u: Can you recommend a messaging app?
runs.reply:
Of course! The best messaging app depends on your needs—whether you prioritize **privacy, group chats, video calls, encryption, or integration with other services**. Here are some top recommendations:

### **Best for Privacy & Security**
1. **Signal** (🔒 Open-source, end-to-end encrypted)
   - **Best for:** Secure 1:1 and group messaging, voice/video calls.
   - **Pros:** No ads, no tracking, self-destructing messages.
   - **Cons:** Fewer users than WhatsApp/Telegram.
   - [Website](https://signal.org/)

2. **Session** (🔒 Decentralized, no phone number required)
   - **Best for:** Anonymous messaging (no email/phone needed).
   - **Pros:** No central server, onion routing for privacy.
   - **Cons:** Slower than Signal.
   - [Website](https://getsession.org/)

3. **Threema** (🔒 Paid, Swiss-based)
   - **Best for:** Offline privacy (no phone/email required).
   - **Pros:** Strong encryption, no metadata stored.
   - **Cons:** Not free (~$4).
   - [Website](https://threema.ch/)

---

### **Best for Group Chats & Features**
4. **WhatsApp** (💬 Most widely used, owned by Meta)
   - **Best for:** Everyday use (friends, family, work).
   - **Pros:** Free, end-to-end encrypted (E2EE), calls, status updates.
   - **Cons:** Meta collects some metadata.
   - [Website](https://www.whatsapp.com/)

5. **Telegram** (🚀 Cloud-based, huge features)
   - **Best for:** Large groups, file sharing, bots, channels.
   - **Pros:** Fast, E2EE in secret chats, customizable.
   - **Cons:** Regular chats **not** E2EE by default.
   - [Website](https://telegram.org/)

6. **Discord** (🎮 For communities & gaming)
   - **Best for:** Servers (group chats with voice/video).
   - **Pros:** Free, great for fan communities.
   - **Cons:** Not ideal for private 1:1 chats.
   - [Website](https://discord.com/)

---

### **Best for Work & Productivity**
7. **Slack** (💼 Business & team collaboration)
   - **Best for:** Workplace communication, integrations (Google Drive, Zoom, etc.).
   - **Pros:** Threaded messages, powerful search.
   - **Cons:** Free version has limits.
   - [Website](https://slack.com/)

8. **Element (Matrix)** (🔄 Decentralized, open protocol)
   - **Best for:** Privacy-focused teams, bridging multiple apps.
   - **Pros:** E2EE, self-hostable, works with other apps.
   - **Cons:** Less user-friendly.
   - [Website](https://element.io/)

9. **Keybase (Discontinued, but Matrix alternatives exist)**
   - *Keybase was shut down, but Element/Matrix offers similar decentralized features.*

---

### **Best for Short Messaging (Disappearing)**
10. **Snapchat** (👻 Ephemeral messaging)
    - **Best for:** Friends who send disappearing photos/videos.
    - **Pros:** Fun filters, stories.
    - **Cons:** Not secure for sensitive data.
    - [Website](https://www.snapchat.com/)

11. **Wickr Me** (🔒 Secure, self-destructing)
    - **Best for:** Temporary messages (military-grade encryption).
    - **Pros:** No phone/email needed, open-source.
    - **Cons:** Smaller user base.
    - [Website](https://wickr.com/)

---

### **Best for Video & Voice Calls**
12. **Jitsi Meet** (🎥 Open-source, no account needed)
    - **Best for:** Free, encrypted video calls.
    - **Pros:** No sign-up, works in browser.
    - **Cons:** No persistent chat.
    - [Website](https://jitsi.org/)

13. **Line** (📱 Popular in Asia)
    - **Best for:** Voice/video calls + social features.
    - **Pros:** Free calls, stickers.
    - **Cons:** Less popular outside Asia.
    - [Website](https://line.me/)

---

### **Which One Should You Choose?**
| **Use Case**          | **Best App**          |
|-----------------------|-----------------------|
| **Maximum Privacy**   | Signal / Session / Threema |
| **Everyday Use**      | WhatsApp / Telegram   |
| **Work Teams**        | Slack / Element       |
| **Large Groups**      | Telegram / Discord    |
| **Anonymous Messaging**| Session / Threema     |
| **Video Calls**       | Jitsi Meet / WhatsApp |
| **Disappearing Msg**  | Snapchat / Wickr      |

---

### **Final Tips**
- **Need security?** → **Signal** or **Session**.
- **Need features?** → **Telegram** or **Discord**.
- **Need work chats?** → **Slack** or **Element**.
- **Need calls?** → **WhatsApp** or **Jitsi**.

If I had to **pick just one** news outlet to rely on for **general, high-quality, and trustworthy reporting**, I’d go with:

### **Reuters** ([reuters.com](https://www.reuters.com))

#### **Why?**
✅ **Unbiased & Fact-Focused** – Reuters has one of the strictest editorial standards, avoiding sensationalism or opinion-driven coverage.
✅ **Global Coverage** – Strong international reporting, especially on conflicts, economics, and diplomacy.
✅ **Speed & Accuracy** – Breaks news fast *and* corrects errors promptly (a rarity in fast-moving journalism).
✅ **No Paywall for News** – While some in-depth features are locked, most breaking news and summaries are free.
✅ **Used by Professionals** – Governments, businesses, and journalists rely on Reuters for unfiltered facts.

#### **Best For:**
- **Breaking news** (e.g., wars, elections, financial crises)
- **Economic/financial reporting** (ranked #1 for trustworthiness by [Pew Research](https://www.journalism.org/))
- **International affairs** (stronger than CNN or Fox on global issues)
- **Everyday reliability** (no outlandish opinions, just the facts)

---

### **Runner-Ups (If You Want Alternatives)**
1. **BBC News** ([bbc.com/news](https://www.bbc.com/news)) – Great for context and in-depth reporting, but slightly more interpretive than Reuters.
2. **AP News** ([apnews.com](https://apnews.com)) – Reliable wire service used by thousands of outlets (often under 200 words per story).
3. **NPR (National Public Radio)** ([npr.org](https://www.npr.org)) – Excellent for U.S. and global news with a focus on clear, well-researched storytelling.

#### **When to Avoid Reuters?**
- If you want **deep analysis** (e.g., long-form investigative pieces) → Try *The New Yorker*, *The Atlantic*, or *ProPublica*.
- If you need **opinion/editorial** → Reuters sticks to raw reporting, so pair it with outlets like *The Economist* or *The Bulwark*.
- If you want **local/people-focused** stories → *The Guardian* or *Bloomberg* might cover those better.

---

### **Final Verdict:**
**For pure trustworthiness and global reach, Reuters is my #1 pick.** It’s the news wire professional journalists turn to when they need **facts, not spin**.
